The human plateau began to budge. The posts flew through the feeds: it was prime time, just before the end of the workday. Two hundred thousand viewers instantly became two hundred and fifty. Online media bots picked up on the event and began churning out stories about the provocative stream by "the most innovative business coach of our generation." And a woman, no less!

Now three hundred and fifty thousand people from all over the world were watching, liking, sharing, and paying real dollars to ask Freya a question. Three hundred and sixty. Three hundred and seventy. Every new thousand took Freya's breath away. And then it was time to answer.

The main thing was not to let this interaction with her followers turn into a group Tinder date.

*"Do you have kids?"* a stranger asked. *"How do you succeed when you have four of them?"*

Freya wanted to answer, *"You don't."* But for one thing, moms on maternity leave made up forty-eight percent of her audience, so it was a sore subject. And for another, you couldn't say that to a follower who had most likely scraped those fifty bucks out of her kids' lunch money. So Freya fell back on a polite, well-rehearsed response.

"Everyone defines success for themselves," she said. "If you've always dreamed of being a mom or a dad, then your children *are* your capital. The key is to stick to your investment strategy and never entrust your capital to unvetted funds."

*"Are you married?"* someone asked, donating the five-dollar minimum.

Questions like that Freya left unanswered. Fortunately, the flood of more interesting (and pricier!) questions flushed all the cheap provocations straight down the toilet.

Besides, her joke had landed. The chat was ecstatic, and the viewer count kept climbing: a clip of her answer had already gone viral on Twitter. Still, fame brings responsibility—the questions took a sharp turn straight into group Tinder date territory.
